_about: Spine of the Standards Cascade: the dated standards events that edges attach to, the coordination milestones and the sovereign branches. Each entry was read on the issuing body's own page on 30 September 2026, with a verbatim excerpt. The relation on each sovereign branch is carried over from the seed as analytical coding; the excerpts confirm only the event and its date.

spine.label: NIST opens its call for post-quantum public-key algorithms, with nominations due by 30 November 2017.

provenance.title: Announcing Request for Nominations for Public-Key Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms
provenance.excerpt: Announcing Request for Nominations for Public-Key Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithms December 20, 2016 ... The purpose of this notice is to announce that nominations for post-quantum candidate algorithms may now be submitted, up until the final deadline of November 30, 2017.
provenance.locator: News item, headline, date and third paragraph

spine.label: NIST selects CRYSTALS-Kyber, CRYSTALS-Dilithium, FALCON and SPHINCS+ for standardisation.

provenance.title: PQC Standardization Process: Announcing Four Candidates to be Standardized, Plus Fourth Round Candidates
provenance.excerpt: PQC Standardization Process: Announcing Four Candidates to be Standardized, Plus Fourth Round Candidates July 05, 2022 ... NIST will recommend two primary algorithms to be implemented for most use cases: CRYSTALS-KYBER (key-establishment) and CRYSTALS-Dilithium (digital signatures). In addition, the signature schemes FALCON and SPHINCS+ will also be standardized.
provenance.locator: News item, headline, date and section 'PQC Standardization'

spine.label: Russia's cryptography standards committee, TC 26, reports that Kodieum, a national post-quantum key exchange, is being discussed and drafted as a methodological recommendation for standardisation.
spine.body: Technical Committee for Standardisation 26, Cryptographic Information Protection (Russia)

provenance.title: В России разработан криптографический механизм, способный выдерживать атаки квантовых компьютеров.
provenance.publisher: Технический комитет по стандартизации «Криптографическая защита информации» (ТК 26)
provenance.excerpt: 29.03.2024 Сотрудники российской компании «Криптонит» разработали криптографический механизм «Кодиеум». ... На данный момент новый механизм проходит процедуры обсуждения и разработки проекта методических рекомендаций по стандартизации. После этого он будет опубликован для открытого обсуждения на сайте ТК26.
provenance.locator: TC 26 site, section 'Новости криптографии' (cryptography news); the item links to CNews as its source

spine.label: The European Commission adopts Recommendation (EU) 2024/1101, asking Member States to agree a coordinated roadmap for the move to post-quantum cryptography.

provenance.title: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2024/1101 of 11 April 2024 on a Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union, L series)
provenance.excerpt: Official Journal of the European Union EN L series 2024/1101 12.4.2024 COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION (EU) 2024/1101 of 11 April 2024 on a Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography

provenance.title: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2024/1101 of 11 April 2024 on a Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (Official Journal of the European Union, L series)

spine.label: NIST publishes its first three post-quantum standards: FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA).

provenance.title: Announcing Approval of Three Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) for Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.excerpt: Announcing Approval of Three Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) for Post-Quantum Cryptography August 13, 2024 ... The Secretary of Commerce has approved three Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS) for post-quantum cryptography: FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard FIPS 204, Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Standard FIPS 205, Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Standard
provenance.locator: News item, headline, date and opening list

spine.label: NIST releases IR 8547 as an initial public draft: quantum-vulnerable algorithms disallowed after 2035, and those at 112-bit strength deprecated after 2030. It was still a draft on 30 September 2026.

provenance.title: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
provenance.excerpt: NIST IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft) Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards ... Date Published: November 12, 2024 Comments Due: January 10, 2025 (public comment period is CLOSED)
provenance.locator: Publication page header

provenance.title: NIST IR 8547 ipd, Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
provenance.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
provenance.excerpt: ECDSA [FIPS186] 112 bits of security strength Deprecated after 2030 Disallowed after 2035
provenance.locator: Section 4.1.1, Table 2 (quantum-vulnerable digital signature algorithms), p. 13; table cells read along the first row

spine.label: South Korea's KpqC competition names four national post-quantum algorithms: AIMer and HAETAE for signatures, NTRU+ and SMAUG-T for key encapsulation.

provenance.title: KpqC Competition Round 2
provenance.excerpt: Selected Algorithms from the KpqC Competition Round 2 (January 16, 2025) After careful consideration during Round 2 of the KpqC competition, the KpqC team is pleased to announce the final algorithms. Round2 candidates Digital Signature PKE/KEM AIMer NTRU+ HAETAE SMAUG-T
provenance.locator: Competition page, Round 2 result announcement and table (columns: Digital Signature, PKE/KEM)

spine.label: China's Institute of Commercial Cryptography Standards launches a global call for next-generation commercial cryptographic algorithms, citing the threat of quantum computing.
spine.body: Institute of Commercial Cryptography Standards (ICCS), China

provenance.title: Announcement on Launching the Next-generation Commercial Cryptographic Algorithms Program (NGCC)
provenance.excerpt: Announcement on Launching the Next-generation Commercial Cryptographic Algorithms Program (NGCC) 2025-02-05 ... In response to the threat of quantum computing and to promote the standardization of the next-generation commercial cryptographic algorithms, the Institute of Commercial Cryptography Standards (ICCS) is launching a global program to call for proposals for next-generation public-key cryptographic algorithms (NGCC-PK)
provenance.locator: English notice, title, date and first sentence

provenance.title: 关于开展新一代商用密码算法征集活动的公告
provenance.excerpt: 关于开展新一代商用密码算法征集活动的公告 2025-02-05 ... 为应对量子计算威胁，推动新一代商用密码算法标准制定，按照密码行业标准化技术委员会工作安排，我院将面向全球陆续开展新一代公钥密码算法、密码杂凑算法、分组密码算法征集活动
provenance.locator: Chinese notice, title, date and first sentence

spine.label: NIST selects HQC as its second post-quantum key-encapsulation mechanism, a backup to ML-KEM.

provenance.title: NIST PQC Standardization Process | HQC Announced as a 4th Round Selection
provenance.excerpt: HQC Announced as a 4th Round Selection March 11, 2025 ... After a thorough evaluation in the Fourth Round of the NIST Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) Standardization Process, NIST has selected HQC for standardization. ... HQC will be the second PQC key-encapsulation mechanism (KEM), following ML-KEM.
provenance.locator: News item, headline, date, first and third paragraphs

provenance.title: NIST Selects HQC as Fifth Algorithm for Post-Quantum Encryption
provenance.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
provenance.excerpt: NIST plans to issue a draft standard incorporating the HQC algorithm in about a year, with a finalized standard expected in 2027.
provenance.locator: News release of March 11, 2025, summary

spine.label: The UK NCSC sets three migration milestones: goals, discovery and an initial plan by 2028, the highest-priority migration by 2031, and full migration by 2035.

provenance.title: Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
provenance.excerpt: The key milestones are: By 2028 Define your migration goals ... By 2031 Carry out your early, highest-priority PQC migration activities ... By 2035 Complete migration to PQC of all your systems, services and products ... Published 20 March 2025 Reviewed 20 March 2025 Version 1.0
provenance.locator: Executive summary and page footer

provenance.title: Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
provenance.excerpt: The PQC algorithms that will be the most widely used were standardised by NIST in 2024: ML-KEM (FIPS 203) ML-DSA (FIPS 204) SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) These supplement two earlier algorithms with a more limited set of uses: LMS, XMSS (NIST SP 800-208)
provenance.locator: Section 'Maturity of PQC technology'

spine.label: EU Member States publish their coordinated roadmap through the NIS Cooperation Group: start the move to post-quantum cryptography by the end of 2026, and protect high-risk uses by the end of 2030.
spine.body: NIS Cooperation Group (EU Member States, supported by the European Commission)

provenance.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
provenance.excerpt: Publication 23 June 2025 The EU Member States, supported by the Commission, issued a roadmap and timeline to start using a more complex form of cybersecurity, the so-called post-quantum cryptography (PQC).
provenance.locator: Library page, publication date and summary

provenance.title: Post-Quantum Cryptography
provenance.publisher: European Commission, Shaping Europe's digital future
provenance.excerpt: adopted the Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography in June 2025. ... All Member States should start transitioning to PQC by the end of 2026. At the same time, the protection of high-risk use cases should be transitioned to PQC as soon as possible, no later than by the end of 2030.
provenance.locator: Policy page, paragraph on the NIS Cooperation Group work stream
